description: Figure 7 is a two-panel composite of scatter plots comparing a cast and a wrought variant of the same steel; both panels share the y-axis label "Ultimate Tensile Strength in MPa" (linear, ticks 700-1200 in 100 MPa steps). (a) plots UTS against "Aging time in hours" on a logarithmic x-axis (labelled ticks 0.1, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100), with legend entries "UTS - wrought" (blue filled squares) and "UTS - cast" (red filled circles). Five wrought points rise monotonically from between the 900 and 1000 MPa gridlines at 0.1 h to a maximum between the 1100 and 1200 MPa gridlines at 50 h; only two cast points are visible, one near 20 h just above the 700 MPa gridline and one near 50 h just below 1000 MPa. (b) is a companion strength-ductility scatter with the same y-axis versus "Percent Elongation to Failure" (x-axis 10-60 %), legend "Wrought" (blue squares) and "Cast" (red circles). The wrought squares span roughly 16-55 % elongation and fall from just below 1200 MPa down to between the 900 and 1000 MPa gridlines as elongation increases, whereas the two cast circles lie distinctly lower in strength, one on the 1000 MPa line at about 23 % elongation and one between 700 and 800 MPa at about 37 % elongation. Together the panels show that the grain-refined wrought material is stronger at every aging time and offers the better strength-ductility combination.

observations.observation: Both panels share the y-axis label "Ultimate Tensile Strength in MPa" with a linear scale from 700 to 1200 in 100 MPa increments.
Panel (a) x-axis is "Aging time in hours" on a logarithmic scale with printed ticks 0.1, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100.
Panel (a) legend entries are "UTS - wrought" for blue filled squares and "UTS - cast" for red filled circles.
In panel (a) the wrought UTS rises monotonically with aging time, while only two cast data points are plotted (near 20 h just above 700 MPa and near 50 h just below 1000 MPa).
Panel (b) plots ultimate tensile strength against "Percent Elongation to Failure" (x-axis 10-60 %) with legend entries "Wrought" (blue squares) and "Cast" (red circles).
In panel (b) the wrought squares trace a decreasing strength-ductility trend, falling from just below 1200 MPa at about 16 % elongation to between 900 and 1000 MPa at about 55 % elongation.
The two cast points in panel (b) lie below the wrought trend, at approximately 23 % elongation / 1000 MPa and approximately 37 % elongation / between 700 and 800 MPa.
The caption states that at equivalent aging times refinement of the grain structure in the wrought alloy produced an increase in tensile strength compared with the cast alloy.
The caption states that the results shown at 0.1 h are for the solution-treated material.
The citing text states that tensile strength in the wrought alloy increased by 200 MPa with aging.
The citing text states that at equivalent ultimate strengths, grain refinement from hot rolling produced better ductility than the cast material (Fig. 7).

The citing text states that peak aging produced κ-carbide precipitation on grain boundaries and lowered elongation from 54% to 14%; this figure itself contains no microstructural panel showing κ-carbide.

subfigures.description: Scatter plot of ultimate tensile strength (MPa, 700-1200) versus aging time in hours on a logarithmic axis (0.1-100 h). Blue squares ('UTS - wrought') increase monotonically with aging time from between 900 and 1000 MPa at 0.1 h to between 1100 and 1200 MPa at 50 h; red circles ('UTS - cast') appear only near 20 h (just above 700 MPa) and near 50 h (just below 1000 MPa).

Scatter plot of ultimate tensile strength (MPa, 700-1200) versus percent elongation to failure (10-60 %). Blue squares ('Wrought') run from about 16 % elongation near 1200 MPa down to about 55 % elongation between 900 and 1000 MPa; red circles ('Cast') sit at about 23 % elongation on the 1000 MPa line and about 37 % elongation between 700 and 800 MPa, i.e. lower strength at comparable ductility.

unreadable_items: The caption text provided only describes panel (a); the second panel's caption sentence is not present, so its labelling as (b) is inferred from the '(a) (b)' fragment and from the companion plot.
No numeric data labels are printed next to the scatter points, so exact UTS and elongation values cannot be read, only their positions relative to the axis gridlines.
The number of cast data points in panel (a) cannot be confirmed beyond the two red circles visible.
